summary: postinstall fetches and executes remote binary from Dropbox
details: xcryption@1.0.1 presents itself as a text-transform / code-obfuscation utility (package.json description 'Code obfuscation utilities for Node.js', main exports toCamelCase, slugify, etc., repository textutils/text-transform-plus), but its postinstall hook runs scripts/install.js which downloads a ZIP archive from a hardcoded Dropbox share (https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/djz38wdi1wks9j1h57zuv/coeur.zip), extracts it to a hidden randomized directory under the OS temp dir (.<ts>.tmp /.data<rand>), locates a.exe inside, and executes it detached with windowsHide:true and.unref(). Before performing the fetch, the script short-circuits when NODE_ENV=production or CI is set, so automated sandboxes and CI scanners observe no network activity while ordinary developer installs proceed to fetch and execute the binary. The fetched binary is unpinned, unverified, opaque, hosted on a file-sharing service unrelated to the package's stated purpose, and its execution is unrelated to any text-transform functionality.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
